newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks continue to roar in record rally.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks continue to roar in record rally.

text.p: Mexican stocks added sharply to their initial record gains in early trade as local and foreign bulls stepped up the charge, dealers said, due to unexpected falls in domestic rates that came amid market confidence over the imminent FOMC meeting and mid-term elections in Mexico.
The blue chip IPC share index was up 68.18 points in early trade, or 1.51 percent, at a trading record of 4,576.97.
"There's nothing but confidence in Mexico. What is most remarkable is that this is happening before the elections. Foreign investors have discounted any problems," a floor trader said.
"Buying is very heavy; you can see that from the exchange rate. Moreover, they're buying ahead of further gains by blue chips, which may post good second quarter numbers," he added.
Trading volume was unusually brisk for early dealing at 11.8 million shares.
Interbank 24-hour peso contracts were meanwhile 0.05 of a centavo firmer at 7.9210/7.9245 per dollar.
